name: N R Narayan Murthy
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; founder of Catamaran Ventures (family investment firm)
profile: Born 1946 in Sidlaghatta, Karnataka, Murthy co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues and Rs 10,000 borrowed from his wife Sudha Murty. He was CEO 1981-2002 and later chairman, and pioneered the Global Delivery Model for IT outsourcing from India. Now chairman emeritus, he invests via Catamaran Ventures and speaks often on entrepreneurship and work culture.
interesting_fact: Time magazine and CNBC have called him the 'father of the Indian IT sector'; Fortune listed him among the 12 greatest entrepreneurs of our time, and he co-chaired the World Economic Forum in Davos in 2005.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and designed and implemented a BASIC interpreter for Electronics Corporation of India Ltd; his first startup, Softronics, folded after roughly a year and a half.
notes: Infosys press is a company route; he holds no executive role. Catamaran Ventures is his personal investment vehicle (no published email found). Father-in-law of Rishi Sunak. Frequent public speaker, so likely receptive to a founder-story podcast.

name: Wang Jianfeng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ningbo Joyson Electronic Corp. (Joyson Electronics), listed in Shanghai (600699) and Hong Kong
profile: Wang founded Ningbo-based Joyson in the early 2000s and turned it into a global auto-parts group through a series of overseas acquisitions after its 2011 listing, including Germany's Preh, US-based KSS and the assets of Japan's Takata. Joyson makes airbags, seatbelts, steering wheels and automotive electronics, and has added a Hong Kong listing and a push into robotics.
interesting_fact: Between 2011 and 2019 Joyson bought nine overseas auto-parts companies, including Preh and KSS, which made a regional supplier into one of the world's largest automotive safety groups.
deep_cut_fact: Wang is an avid photographer whose work has been exhibited at the Ningbo Museum of Art. Before Joyson he was general manager of TRW (Ningbo) Electronic Components Fastener Co. and Ningbo Yongxing Vehicle Parts Co.
notes: Also known in English as Jeff Wang. The photography detail comes from the Forbes bio; the TRW/Yongxing career detail comes from the GlobalData executive profile (https://www.globaldata.com/company-profile/ningbo-joyson-electronic-corp/executives/). Sources disagree on Joyson's founding year (2001 vs 2004). The robotics push is relevant to the podcast's tech angle.

name: Tuncay Ozilhan
current_role: Former Chairman of Anadolu Group (handed the chair to Kamil Süleyman Yazıcı on 21 April 2025); Chairman of the Anadolu Foundation per the group's board page
profile: Born in Kayseri in 1947, Özilhan is the son of Anadolu Group co-founder İzzet Özilhan. He was the group's CEO from 1984 to 2017 and its chairman from 2007 to April 2025, building it into a conglomerate spanning Anadolu Efes beer, Coca-Cola İçecek bottling, Migros retail and Isuzu/Honda automotive. He handed the chair to the third generation in 2025.
interesting_fact: Under the group's founding 'constitution', Anadolu donates 1-5% of profits to the Anadolu Foundation before any dividends are paid. The foundation runs a hospital, a school and dormitories.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1977 as general director of Erciyas Brewery in his home region and held posts at Toz Metal and Turkish Airlines before joining Anadolu Group in 1984. He later served as chairman of the business association TÜSİAD (2001-2003).
notes: Stepped down as group chairman in April 2025, so 'current role' may be limited to foundation and board posts. Sources differ between 'chairman' and 'president' of TÜSİAD and give 2001-2003 or 2001-2004 for the term. No dedicated press email found; Kaan Ünver is named as the group's corporate communications coordinator.

name: Philip O'Doherty
current_role: Chairman and owner of Derry City FC; founder and former CEO of E&I Engineering (now part of Vertiv)
profile: An engineer and Queen's University Belfast graduate, O'Doherty founded E&I Engineering in Burnfoot, Co. Donegal in the 1980s. It made switchgear and power-distribution equipment, much of it for data centres. In 2021 he sold it with affiliate Powerbar Gulf to Vertiv for about $1.8bn upfront plus up to $200m earnout, in cash and Vertiv stock. He now bankrolls Derry City FC.
interesting_fact: At the time of the sale E&I had about 2,100 employees, roughly $460m in sales and over 1,000 staff at its rural Burnfoot HQ, making it one of the largest private employers in the Donegal/Derry border region and a key supplier of data-centre power infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting E&I he spent five years as an engineer at DuPont's plant in Campsie, Co. Derry. He has long been the financial backbone of his hometown club Derry City FC and in recent seasons set an explicit target of winning the club's first league title in decades.
notes: Forbes data says 'Vertix'; the acquirer is Vertiv. Highly relevant to a data-centre/energy podcast. Sources give the founding year as 1986 or 1987; the DuPont detail is from the Forbes bio (https://www.forbes.com/profile/philip-odoherty/). Low media profile outside football; the club is the most realistic route. No published personal or office email found.

name: Qin Hui
current_role: Former controlling shareholder of Stellar Megamedia / SMI Holdings Group (星美控股), a Chinese cinema chain; no confirmed current role
profile: Qin Hui (覃辉), a Chongqing-born businessman, built the Stellar (星美) cinema and media group, one of China's larger theatre circuits in the 2010s, listed in Hong Kong as SMI Holdings. His brother Qin Hong ran day-to-day operations. Forbes listed him at #1339 on its 2018 billionaires list (Media & Entertainment). The group fell into a debt and cash-flow crisis from late 2018.
interesting_fact: Stellar was among the earliest private cinema chains to expand nationwide after China's film-distribution reforms. In 2010 SMI agreed to buy 25 cinemas directly from Qin Hui for HK$55m.
notes: The Forbes profile (forbes.com/profile/qin-hui) links him to SMI Holdings Group; he is NOT the historian Qin Hui (秦晖). Recent coverage is mostly negative: a 2018 CSRC 5-year securities-market ban over the listed unit Shengleda, and Stellar's debt crisis. Last on the Forbes list in 2018. No reachable public contacts found. Low priority for outreach.

name: Shigenobu Nagamori
current_role: Chairman, Nagamori Gakuen Educational Foundation (operator of Kyoto University of Advanced Science); fully retired from Nidec in Feb 2026
profile: Nagamori founded Nidec (Nippon Densan) in Kyoto in 1973 and built it into the world's largest maker of HDD and precision motors, growing it through dozens of acquisitions and later pushing into EV traction motors. He was president for 45 years. He left the Nidec board in December 2025 and gave up the chairman emeritus title in February 2026. He now focuses on Kyoto University of Advanced Science.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he took over a Kyoto university, renamed it Kyoto University of Advanced Science (KUAS), and built an English-taught engineering program to tackle Japan's shortage of motor and mechatronics engineers. Commentators called it the latest in his string of acquisitions.
deep_cut_fact: Nidec started on 23 July 1973 with ¥20m of capital and three co-founders. A month later Nagamori rented the first floor of a two-storey house by the Katsura River in Kyoto's Ukyo ward as the first 'Katsura Factory' to make small precision AC motors.
notes: He left Nidec completely in Feb 2026 amid an accounting scandal at a subsidiary (TSE 'special alert' designation); avoid that topic in outreach. KUAS is now the best route and the natural angle (engineering education, motors/EVs). The Nagamori Foundation (motor/actuator/generator research awards) is a separate body: https://www.nidec.com/en/nagamori-f/about/

name: Zhu Hai
current_role: Actual controller (largest shareholder) of Shenzhen Bioeasy Biotechnology (易瑞生物, SZSE 300942); founding chairman
profile: Zhu Hai (朱海), a PhD-trained scientist born in 1973, founded Shenzhen Bioeasy, a maker of rapid food-safety tests (immunochromatographic strips and analysers) that has expanded into point-of-care diagnostics. Its products are used in food safety, drug, infectious-disease and public-safety testing. Bioeasy listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in February 2021 with Sequoia China backing. Zhu remains the controlling shareholder via Yirui (Hainan) Venture Capital.
interesting_fact: Bioeasy's 2021 listing was Sequoia China's first IPO in food-safety testing. At the IPO Zhu said his goal was to use the capital markets to build 'a world-class food safety company'.
notes: The 2026 interim report lists Xiao Zhaoli (肖昭理) as legal representative, so Zhu may no longer be chairman; he is still named actual controller. Press reports (c. 2021) say he was deputy lab director at the Shenzhen Entry-Exit Inspection & Quarantine Bureau food testing centre (2004-10) before founding Bioeasy. Not verified here (search budget exhausted), so it is not used as the deep-cut fact. Avoid personal/family topics.

name: Alfred Mann
profile: Alfred E. Mann was an American physicist and serial medical-device entrepreneur. He founded Spectrolab (solar cells), Pacesetter Systems (pacemakers), MiniMed (insulin pumps), Advanced Bionics (cochlear implants) and Second Sight, and led MannKind. He died in 2016.
notes: Deceased; source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_E._Mann. Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Rama Prasad Goenka
profile: R. P. Goenka founded the RPG Group (RPG Enterprises, 1979), the diversified Indian conglomerate now chaired by his son Harsh Goenka; the group later split with the separately run RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group. He died in 2013.
notes: Deceased; source https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rama_Prasad_Goenka. Rest skipped. The successor groups (RPG Enterprises: Harsh Goenka; RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group: Sanjiv Goenka) are separate potential targets.

name: Robert Mouawad
current_role: Head of the Robert Mouawad real-estate group and Robert Mouawad Foundation/Private Museum; former president of Mouawad jewellers (retired 2010)
profile: A third-generation jeweller, Mouawad took over the house his grandfather founded in Beirut in 1890. He moved its headquarters to Geneva in the 1970s and built it into a global high-jewellery and watch brand known for buying some of the world's largest diamonds. He handed the business to his sons in 2010 and now focuses on real estate, including Reef Island in Bahrain and a 2024 Riyadh project with Dar Global, and on his museum.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he opened the Robert Mouawad Private Museum in a neo-Gothic Beirut palace built in 1891 by collector Henri Philippe Pharaoun. It displays Roman and Byzantine antiquities, Islamic woodwork, icons and rare books, and reopened after the 2020 Beirut port explosion.
deep_cut_fact: He originally studied in Europe to become a doctor, until his father persuaded him to join the family business, where he started as a salesman. The Gemological Institute of America's Carlsbad, California campus is named in his honour for his support of GIA.
notes: Born c.1944 and still listed by Forbes; there is no death report, but this was not separately verified. The mouawad.com site blocked automated reads, so no press contact was captured. The company (now run by his sons Fred, Alain and Pascal) is the likely route. The Bahrain/Riyadh real-estate projects are the most podcast-relevant angle.

name: Mori Arkin
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Arkin Capital (Israeli multi-asset investor; formerly Arkin Holdings); controlling shareholder of Sol-Gel Technologies
profile: Born in Ramat Gan in 1952, Arkin took over his father's small pharmaceutical importer Agis at 19 after his father's death in 1972. He turned it into a generic-drug manufacturer and sold it to Perrigo in 2004 for about $818m. He now runs Arkin Capital, which manages over $2.5bn across health, tech, private equity and real estate, and controls Nasdaq-listed dermatology firm Sol-Gel.
interesting_fact: He was a 19-year-old serving soldier when he inherited the running of Agis. Forbes later dubbed him a 'pharma kingpin-turned-VC' when he joined the billionaires' club in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: He started university at Tel Aviv studying Old Testament and archaeology before switching to psychology (BA with honours), then did graduate work in physiological psychology and philosophy of science. He is also an art-history buff who composes music as a hobby.
notes: The music/art hobby comes from Forbes facts (https://www.forbes.com/profile/mori-arkin/). Arkin Capital (formerly Arkin Holdings; the old domain redirects) is his own office, so its contact form is the best route. Also co-founder and chairman of Accelmed. Avoid family/children topics.

name: Li Xuhui
current_role: Shareholder of Foshan Haitian Flavouring and Food; former director and vice president (left 2016)
profile: Li Xuhui is a long-time executive and shareholder of Foshan Haitian Flavouring & Food, China's largest soy-sauce maker. She was a director and vice president until 2016, and her fortune comes from her Haitian stake. Haitian chairman Pang Kang and vice chairman Cheng Xue are also billionaires.
interesting_fact: She managed Haitian's oyster-sauce factory from 1999 to 2010 before serving as a company director and vice president.
notes: Very private, with no public role since 2016. Her Chinese name was not verified (search budget exhausted). Haitian's IR office (SSE 603288 / HKEX filings) is the only institutional route, but she no longer works there. Low priority.

name: Malav Ashwin Dani
current_role: Managing Director, Hitech Corporation Ltd (Dani family plastic-packaging group); member of the Asian Paints promoter (Dani) family
profile: Malav Dani is the son of the late Ashwin Dani, a long-time leader of Asian Paints, the paint company co-founded in a Mumbai garage in 1942 by four friends including his grandfather Suryakant Dani. His wealth derives mainly from the family's Asian Paints stake. He runs Hitech Corporation, a rigid plastic packaging maker founded in 1991 with 13 locations in India and a technology centre in Pune.
interesting_fact: Asian Paints began in February 1942 in a garage in Girgaon, Mumbai, started by four friends: Champaklal Choksey, Chimanlal Choksi, Suryakant Dani and Arvind Vakil. Their families still hold the controlling promoter stake.
deep_cut_fact: On Hitech's website Malav Dani sums up his management philosophy as: 'Adopting Six Sigma, we enhance customer satisfaction while embracing sustainability and global unity through Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (the Sanskrit idea that 'the world is one family').
notes: His Asian Paints board status was not verified (search budget exhausted). His father Ashwin Dani died in September 2023. contact@hitechgroup.com is Hitech's general corporate inbox, not a personal address. Hitech's chairperson is his mother, Ina Dani (Hitech Specialities).

name: Zhang Shengwei
current_role: Founder and majority owner, Shenzhen iMiracle Technology (maker of Elf Bar and Lost Mary vapes)
profile: Zhang Shengwei founded Shenzhen iMiracle Technology, part of the Heaven Gifts group, whose Elf Bar brand (launched 2018) became the world's best-selling disposable e-cigarette by 2023, alongside sister brand Lost Mary. He also holds stakes in the firms behind Air Bar and Geekvape. He keeps an extremely low public profile.
interesting_fact: iMiracle was expected to generate up to $4bn in revenue in 2023. In the UK alone, Elf Bar and Lost Mary sold more than £900m of vapes in 12 months, according to NielsenIQ.
deep_cut_fact: Before vaping, Zhang was a cross-border e-commerce seller who sold kitchenware and clothing on eBay.
notes: Very private, with almost no interviews. The brand's PR inbox is the only published route. The vaping industry is under heavy regulatory scrutiny (UK disposable-vape ban, US FDA actions); be mindful of framing in outreach.
